questions.question: What is represented by the product of force with displacement in the direction of force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work**__.

__
 
• **Work **is the **product **of the **component **of the **force **in the **direction **of the **displacement **and the **magnitude **of this **displacement**.

 
 
• For work to be done, in a scientific sense, a **force **must be **exerted **and there must be **displacement **in the **direction **of the **force**.
 
• **Mathematically **it is represented
 
• The** SI unit** of work is the **joule **(J), which is defined as the work done by a force of 1 Newton in moving an object through a distance of 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is conventionally given the **symbol J **and **expressed **in **Newton**-**seconds**.
 
 
 
• Power is the rate at which work is done.
 
 
• The** SI unit** of power is **Watt **(W) 
 
• **Power **= **Work / time **

questions.question: For which of the following quantities does the unit of time appear twice in the denominator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is the **rate of change of the velocity** of an object with respect to time.
 
• Acceleration is a **vector quantity** (has magnitude and direction both).
 
• The unit of **acceleration** is **meter per second square**(m/s²) or **LT⁻²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **speed** of an object is the magnitude of the** rate of change of its position with time**, it is thus a **scalar quantity**.

 
 
• Unit of speed is meter per second (**m/s**) or LT⁻¹.
 
 
 
• A **displacement** is a vector whose length is the **shortest distance** from the initial to the final position of a point undergoing motion.
 
 
• Unit of displacement is **meter** (**m**).
 
 
 
• The **velocity** of an object is the **rate of change of its position** **with respect to a frame of reference** and is a function of time.
 
• Velocity is equivalent to a specification of an object's speed and direction of motion.
 
• It is a vector quantity.** **
 
 
• **Unit **of velocity is meter per second (**m/s**) or **LT⁻¹**.

questions.question: Kinetic and potential energies of a body are the components of its ______ energy.

• Mechanical Energy:
 
 
• The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy is called mechanical energy.
 
• From the above, it is clear that the total mechanical energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy.
 
 

 
• **Potential Energy:**

 
 
• The energy of an object obtained by doing work against conservative forces like spring force and gravitational force is called potential energy.
 
• The potential energy of an object at a height from the ground is given as:
 
 
• **P = mgh**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• The energy obtained by an object by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.
 
 
• **KE = (1)/(2) times mv²**
 
 
 
• K is kinetic energy, v is the speed of the object, and m is the mass of the object.

questions.question: What is the unit of energy in the International System of Units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Energy is explained by work, accordingly **the SI unit of energy is the same as the unit of work – the joule (J).**
 
• This is the **basic energy unit of the metric system**, or in a later more broad formulation, **the International System of Units (SI). **
 
• It is eventually explained in **terms of the meter, kilogram, and second.**
 
• **1 Joule (J) is the MKS unit of energy**, equal to the force of one Newton acting through one meter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celsius** is presently a derived unit for temperature in the SI system, kelvin being the base unit.
 
• **The kelvin**, symbol K, is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature.
 
• **Fahrenheit **is a scale work for measuring temperature based on the freezing and boiling points of water. ​

questions.question: A person weighs 60 kg on the ground. When his weight is measured in a lift moving vertically upwards with uniform acceleration then the weight of the person will:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**measure greater than 60 units**__

__Concept__:

The apparent weight of a person inside a lift

__
 
• When the lift moves upward with acceleration *a*. Then the net upward force on the person is-

R - mg = ma

∴ Apparent weight, R = mg + ma = m (g + a)

So, when a lift accelerates upwards, the apparent weight of the person inside it increases.

 
• When the lift moves downwards with acceleration *a*. Then the net downward force on the person is-

Mg - R = ma

∴ Apparent weight, R = mg - ma = m (g - a)

So, when a lift accelerates downwards, the apparent weight of the person inside it decreases.

 
• When the lift is at rest or moving with uniform velocity v downward/upward. The acceleration *a* = 0, then the net force on the person is-

R - mg = m x 0 = 0

R = mg

∴ Apparent weight = Actual weight

 
• When the lift falls freely. If the supporting cable of the lift breaks, the lift falls freely under gravity. Then *a = g*. The net downward force on the person is -

R = m(g - g) = 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1eb6260b1078371d1cd1b7252a716640ed1835ae02e7796d2a67f39c5c02539.png] 

 
• Thus, the apparent weight of the man becomes zero. This is because both the man and the lift are moving downwards with same acceleration *‘g’* and so there are no forces of action and reaction between the person and the lift. Hence a person develops a feeling of weightlessness when he falls freely under gravity.
 
• Newton's second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly related to the net force and inversely related to its mass.
 
 
• The acceleration of an object depends on two things, force and mass.
 
 

F = ma

Where F = force acting on body, m = mass of body, a = acceleration.

Calculation__:

Given: mass = m, a = 2g N = ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e593c97fb1e2c7dfa06466a6b13d3d2cd0c950014965960dfb384e871b06471.png] 

According to Newtons 2nd law of motion,

ΣF = Ma

N - Mg = 3Mg

N = 4 Mg

Reaction on the floor by the man is 4 mg and vertically upward in direction.

questions.question: The SI unit of the power of a lens is denoted by the letter _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Dioptre__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Power is the ability to bend light and it is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens/mirror in meters.
 
• Power (P) = 1/f
 
• Where f is the focal length of the lens/mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dioptre is a unit of measurement of the optical power of a lens or curved mirror, which is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length measured in metres.
 
• And since the S.I unit of the focal length is the meter (m).
 
• So the S.I unit of power =** 1/(SI unit of focal length) = m-1 = Dioptre (D).**
 
• **1 m-1 = 1 D**

questions.question: Which of the following devices converts chemical energy into electrical energy ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy.
 
• The chemical reactions in a battery involve the flow of electrons from one material (electrode) to another, through an external circuit.
 
• The flow of electrons provides an electric current that can be used to do work. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A generator converts the mechanical (kinetic) energy of the rotor to electrical energy.
 
• A dynamo also called an electric generator, is simply a machine that converts mechanical energy into electricity. Dynamos are most often found inside power plants.

questions.question: The ‘to and fro’ or ‘back and forth’ motion of an object is termed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vibration.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vibration **is the mechanical oscillations of an object about an equilibrium point.
 
• The oscillations may be regular such as the motion of a pendulum or random such as the movement of a tire on a gravel road. 
 
• Vibration enters the body from the part of the body or organ in contact with vibrating equipment.
 
• When a worker operates hand-held equipment such as a chain saw or jackhammer, vibration affects hands and arms.
 
• Such exposure is called hand-arm vibration exposure.
 
• When a worker sits or stands on a vibrating floor or seat, the vibration exposure affects almost the entire body and is called whole-body vibration exposure.​​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impulse:**

 
 
• Impulse is a term that quantifies the overall effect of a force acting over time. It is conventionally given the symbol ' J' and expressed in Newton seconds.
 
• For a constant force, **J = F⋅Δt**
 
 

 
• **Convulsions:**

 
 
• A convulsion occurs when a person's muscles contract uncontrollably.
 
• They can continue for a few seconds or many minutes. 
 
• A convulsion might obstruct a person's airway, leading to suffocation.
 
 
 
• **Swing:**
 
 
• Swing is an example of simple harmonic motion because
 
• It has to and fro motion or the back and forth repetitive movements along the same line and about a mean position.

questions.question:
Which of the following equation of motion is correct?

I. v = (u/2) + at

II. s = 2ut + at²
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***v = u + at*** is the first equation of motion.

 
 
• It is the equation of motion-time relation__.
 
• In this ​v=u+at equation,
 __
 
• u is the initial velocity
 
• v is the final velocity
 
• a is acceleration
 
• t is the time period
 
 
 
• The given equation is derived from the acceleration point of view. (It can also be derived from velocity and time graphs)
 
 
 
• ***s = ut + 1over2 at²***

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8e6412eaa10e855ffc4fb5c50220b89d8165c04af44bd58fcf4a3d95e0d6e7a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• In the case of uniform acceleration, there are three equations of motion which are also known as the laws of constant acceleration.
 
• The three equations are,
 
 
• ​v=u+at
 
• v² = u² + 2as\ or \ v² - u² = 2as​
 
• s = ut + {1over{2}}at² 
 
 
 
• where, s = displacement; u = initial velocity; v = final velocity; a = acceleration; t = time of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• These equations are referred to as SUVAT equations where SUVAT stands for displacement (s), initial velocity (u), final velocity (v), acceleration (a) and time (T).​

questions.question: The rate of change in the velocity of an object per unit time is referred as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**acceleration.**__

• The rate of change in the velocity of an object per unit time is referred as** acceleration.**
 
• When the velocity of a moving object changes either in magnitude or in direction or in both, then the body is said to be in acceleration.
 
• The rate of change in velocity is called acceleration.
 
• ⇒ a =(Δ v)/(Δ t)
 
• Where Δv = change in velocity/speed and Δt = time

• **Average velocity **is a vector quantity. Average velocity is defined as the change in position or displacement (∆x) divided by the time intervals (∆t) in which the displacement occurs.
